dimensions.assessment: Affects Department of State personnel, international visitors, athletes, host cities, and foreign relations stakeholders.
dimensions.evidence: The Office of Sports Diplomacy... is established in the Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs of the Department of State.

dimensions.assessment: Establishes administrative planning, reporting, and coordination duties within the Department of State rather than altering domestic laws or benefits.
dimensions.evidence: require a sports diplomacy strategy to strategically leverage the major sporting events being hosted in the United States

dimensions.assessment: Requires assigning personnel and providing implementation support within the Department of State, but specifies no direct new funding amounts.
dimensions.evidence: a description of the financial and personnel support needed to implement the 5-year sports diplomacy strategy

dimensions.assessment: Directs executive branch strategy development, interagency coordination, visa process coordination, and annual reporting to congressional committees.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act... the Secretary of State shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees a 5-year sports diplomacy strategy

dimensions.assessment: Temporary organizational and reporting mandates tied to international sporting events taking place between 2024 and 2034, with a 10-year sunset.
dimensions.evidence: This section shall cease to have effect beginning on the date that is 10 years after the date of the enactment of this Act.

missing_information: Specific cost estimates for implementing the sports diplomacy strategies are not stated.
Exact budget reallocations for the new office staff are not detailed.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill requires the Department of State to develop a 10-year sports diplomacy strategy, establishes an Office of Sports Diplomacy, and mandates regular implementation reports.
